_comment: Each feature in this file is a triple: a behaviour, which is a plain-language description of what the feature must do; a verification_command, which is the exact command that proves the behaviour works; and a state, which records where the feature stands. The allowed states are not_started, active, blocked, and passing. The gating rule is that a feature moves from active to passing only when its verification_command succeeds, so a feature is never marked passing by hand, by guess, or because the code looks finished. This explanation lives in the _comment field so the file stays valid JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) that a script can read.

features.behaviour: When a user searches for a word that appears in an item title, the search endpoint returns every item whose title contains that word, and it returns no item whose title does not contain it.
When a user searches with an empty query, the search endpoint returns the full list of items instead of an error, so an empty search behaves like browsing the catalogue.
When a user searches for a word that matches nothing, the search endpoint returns an empty list with a successful response, rather than an error or a misleading result.
